q: Stairs serving an occupant load of 50 shall have a minimum width of?
n: Stairways serving 50 or fewer occupants may be 900 mm wide. Over 50 requires 1.10 m. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule XII, Sec. 1207.5.a.

q: Maximum riser height for new stairs
n: For new stairs the Fire Code limits risers to 180 mm and requires treads of at least 280 mm. The NBC uses 200 mm and 250 mm. Source: RIRR of RA 9514 (Fire Code, 2019), Table 2 (Dimensional Criteria for New Stairs).

q: A designer is evaluating a stair that must comply with all applicable Philippine laws, including the National Building Code (NBCP), the Fire Code IRR, and the Amended BP 344 IRR. What is the prevailing maximum allowable riser height that satisfies the most restrictive requirement among these laws?
n: The limits are 200 mm (NBC), 180 mm (Fire Code) and 150 mm (2024 amended BP 344, for accessible stairs). The most restrictive is 150 mm. Source: NBC IRR Sec. 1207.5.b; Fire Code RIRR Table 2; Amended IRR of BP 344 (2024), Stairs.

q: Minimum tread depth for new stairs
n: The Fire Code's minimum tread depth for new stairs is 280 mm. Source: RIRR of RA 9514 (Fire Code, 2019), Table 2.

q: A stair must comply simultaneously with the National Building Code (NBCP), the Fire Code IRR, and the Amended BP 344 IRR. What is the prevailing minimum allowable tread depth based on the most restrictive requirement among these laws?
n: The minimums are 250 mm (NBC), 280 mm (Fire Code) and 300 mm (2024 amended BP 344, accessible stairs). The most restrictive is 300 mm. Source: NBC IRR Sec. 1207.5.b; Fire Code RIRR Table 2; Amended IRR of BP 344 (2024), Stairs.

q: According to the National Building Code of the Philippines (PD 1096), what is the maximum vertical distance allowed between landings in a flight of stairs to ensure safe and accessible movement within buildings, particularly in multi-level structures where uninterrupted risers may compromise user safety?
n: There may be no more than 3.60 m of vertical distance between landings. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule XII, Sec. 1207.5.g.

q: Under the National Building Code of the Philippines (PD 1096), what is the minimum clear width required for the main entrance door of a building intended for general occupancy, ensuring safe and unobstructed access for users and complying with standard building regulations?
n: Every required exit doorway must fit a door at least 900 mm wide and 2.00 m high. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule XII, Sec. 1207.3.c.

q: For buildings of more than one-storey, the minimum ceiling height of the first storey shall be how many meters?
n: In buildings of more than one storey, the first storey needs a ceiling height of at least 2.70 m and the second 2.40 m. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule VIII, Sec. 805.1.

q: A proposed two-storey residential dwelling uses artificial ventilation for all habitable rooms. Under Section 805 of the IRR of the National Building Code of the Philippines, what is the minimum allowable ceiling height for habitable rooms that rely on artificial ventilation?
n: Habitable rooms with artificial ventilation need ceiling heights of at least 2.40 m. Naturally ventilated rooms need 2.70 m. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule VIII, Sec. 805.1.

q: A homeowner plans to add a mezzanine inside a two-storey residential dwelling to serve as a compact study loft. Under Section 805 of the IRR of the National Building Code of the Philippines, what is the minimum clear ceiling height required both above and below this residential mezzanine?
n: Mezzanine floors need a clear ceiling height of at least 1.80 m above and below. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule VIII, Sec. 805.2.

q: In the context of residential design governed by the National Building Code of the Philippines, which of the following minimum floor areas applies specifically to a room intended for human habitation—excluding kitchens, bathrooms, and utility spaces—and is enforceable regardless of housing typology or subsidy classification?
n: A room for human habitation must be at least 6.00 m² with a least dimension of 2.00 m. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule VIII, Sec. 806.1.a.

q: Minimum dimension of a habitable room
n: The least dimension of a habitable room is 2.00 m. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule VIII, Sec. 806.1.a.

q: Least dimension for a kitchen
n: A kitchen must be at least 3.00 m² with a least dimension of 1.50 m. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule VIII, Sec. 806.1.b.

q: Minimum area for a kitchen
n: Under the NBC, a kitchen must have a minimum area of 3.00 m², with a least dimension of 1.50 m. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule VIII, Sec. 806.1.b.

q: Under the National Building Code of the Philippines (NBCP), what is the minimum allowable least dimension for a standard toilet and bath?
n: A bath and toilet must be at least 1.20 m² with a least dimension of 900 mm. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule VIII, Sec. 806.1.c.

q: A proposed residential unit includes a compact bath and toilet intended only for basic sanitary use. Under Section 806 of the IRR of the National Building Code of the Philippines, what is the minimum allowable floor area for a bath and toilet?
n: The minimum floor area for a bath and toilet is 1.20 m². Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule VIII, Sec. 806.1.c.

q: Every room not provided with artificial ventilation shall be provided with a window or windows with a total free area of opening equal to at least how many percent of the floor area of the room?
n: Rooms without artificial ventilation need windows with a free opening area of at least 10% of the floor area, and not less than 1.00 m². Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule VIII, Sec. 808.1.

q: A proposed residential building includes a vertical vent shaft serving interior toilet rooms. Under Section 809 of the IRR of the National Building Code of the Philippines, what is the minimum allowable least dimension of a vent shaft?
n: No vent shaft may have a least dimension below 600 mm. Its area must be at least 1.00 m² per meter of height, and never less than 1.00 m². Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule VIII, Sec. 809.1.

q: Due to the limited space under the stairs, a toilet and bath (T&B) is designed at the minimum floor area allowed by the code. Under NBCP Section 808 on window openings for naturally ventilated rooms, what is the minimum required window area for this T&B?
n: Toilets and baths need window area of at least 1/20 of the floor area: 1.20 m² ÷ 20 = 0.06 m². This is above the 240 mm² floor. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule VIII, Secs. 806.1.c and 808.1.

q: Mezzanine floors shall have a clear ceiling height of not less than how many meters above and below it?
n: Mezzanine floors need a clear ceiling height of at least 1.80 m above and below. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule VIII, Sec. 805.2.

q: Minimum air space requirement for school rooms
o: 3 cubic meters with 1 sqm floor area per person
2 cubic meters with 1 sqm floor area per person
n: School rooms need 3.00 m³ of air space with 1.00 m² of floor area per person. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule VIII, Sec. 807.1.a.

q: Minimum air space requirement for habitable rooms
o: 3 cubic meters with 1 sqm floor area per person
2 cubic meters with 1 sqm floor area per person
n: Habitable rooms need 14.00 m³ of air space per person. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule VIII, Sec. 807.1.c.

q: Minimum air space requirement for workshops, factories and offices
o: 2 cubic meters with 1 sqm floor area per person
3 cubic meters with 1 sqm floor area per person
n: Workshops, factories and offices need 12.00 m³ of air space per person. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule VIII, Sec. 807.1.b.

q: An apartment or residential condominium of five (5) storeys or more shall have how many elevators on twenty-four (24) hour constant service?
n: Apartments or residential condominiums of five storeys or more must keep at least one passenger elevator in 24-hour constant service. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule XIV (Elevators), item i.

q: Accessible elevators shall have a minimum dimension of:
n: The 2024 amended IRR sets the accessible elevator car at 1,200 mm wide × 1,400 mm deep with a 900 mm door. The older IRR allowed 1.10 m × 1.40 m. Source: Amended IRR of BP 344 (2024), Appendix C, Accessible Elevators.

q: Accessible elevators should be located not more than how many meters from the entrance?
n: Accessible elevators must be no more than 30.00 m from the building entrance. Source: BP 344 IRR, Elevators.

q: Under the Revised IRR of BP 344, at what height from the finished floor should the Accessible Elevator Car Operating Panel (COP) be installed?
n: The Accessible Elevator Car Operating Panel is installed 900 mm on center from the floor. Source: Amended IRR of BP 344 (2024), Appendix C, Item 8.7.a.

q: According to the Revised Implementing Rules and Regulations of BP 344. accessible elevator cars shall be provided with handrails installed at what height above the finished floor level, measured to the top of the handrail?
n: Handrails in accessible elevator cars are placed 900 mm from the finished floor to the top of the rail, on both sides and at the rear. Source: Amended IRR of BP 344 (2024), Appendix C, Item 8.6.a.

q: According to accessibility standards for elevator cars, what is the minimum required clear door opening to accommodate persons with disabilities?
n: Accessible elevator cars must have a clear door opening of at least 900 mm. Source: Amended IRR of BP 344 (2024), Appendix C, Accessible Elevators (car 1,400 mm deep × 1,200 mm wide, door ≥ 900 mm).

q: A vertical platform lift is provided as an accessible means of overcoming a change in level in accordance with BP 344. What is the minimum clear door opening required for the lift to accommodate wheelchair users?
n: A platform lift needs a clear door opening of at least 900 mm. Source: Amended IRR of BP 344 (2024), Appendix C, Item 9.2.a.

q: A vertical platform lift is provided to overcome a change in level where the installation of a full passenger elevator is impractical. Under BP 344 accessibility standards, what is the minimum maneuvering space that should be provided at the entrance and exit of the lift to allow a wheelchair user to safely approach, enter, exit, and turn?
n: A platform lift needs a clear maneuvering space at least 1,500 mm wide by 1,500 mm deep, measured from the face of the door. Source: Amended IRR of BP 344 (2024), Appendix C, Item 9.2.a.

q: Elevator lobbies shall have a minimum clear space of at least
n: Elevator lobbies need a clear space of at least 1,800 × 1,800 mm. Source: Amended IRR of BP 344 (2024), Appendix C, Item 8.11.

q: A canopy or marquee is a permanent roofed structure above a door attached to and supported by the building and projecting over a wall or sidewalk. This includes any object or decoration attached thereto. Under the National Building Code of the Philippines and its IRR, what is the minimum horizontal clearance required between the outermost edge of a marquee and the curb line?
n: The outermost edge of a marquee must be at least 300 mm from the curb line, and its underside at least 3.00 m above the pavement. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule X, Sec. 1005.2.

q: The vertical clearance between the pavement and the underside of projections over streets or sidewalks
n: The clearance between the street or sidewalk grade and the lowest underside of a balcony or appendage projecting over a street must be at least 3.00 m. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule X, Sec. 1003.2.

q: Width of planting strip and sidewalk if the ROW is 10 m
n: For a 10 m right-of-way, BP 220 provides a 0.80 m planting strip and a 1.20 m sidewalk. Source: BP 220 Revised IRR, Table 6 (Planting Strip and Sidewalk Widths).

q: The act of conceiving, choosing and developing the type, disposition, arrangement and proportioning of the structural elements of an architectural work, giving due consideration to safety, cost-effectiveness, functionality, and aesthetics
n: Structural conceptualization is conceiving, choosing and developing the type, disposition, arrangement and proportioning of the structural elements of an architectural work, with due regard to safety, cost-effectiveness, functionality and aesthetics. Source: RA 9266, Sec. 3 (definition of Structural Conceptualization).

q: Detailed planning and design of the indoor/enclosed areas of any proposed building/structure, including retrofit, renovation, rehabilitation or expansion work.
n: Architectural interiors is the detailed planning and design of the indoor or enclosed areas of a building, including retrofit, renovation, rehabilitation or expansion work. Source: RA 9266, Sec. 3 (definition of Architectural Interiors).

q: Which specialized architectural service is primarily concerned with controlling sound quality, speech intelligibility, reverberation, noise transmission, and overall acoustic performance within buildings and enclosed spaces?
n: Architectural acoustics is the specialized service that controls sound quality, speech intelligibility, reverberation and noise transmission in buildings. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 203 (Specialized Architectural Services).

q: Which specialized architectural service is primarily concerned with the planning, selection, placement, and control of natural and artificial lighting to enhance visual comfort, aesthetics, functionality, and energy efficiency within the built environment?
n: Architectural lighting design covers the planning, selection, placement and control of natural and artificial lighting for comfort, aesthetics, function and energy efficiency. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 203 (Specialized Architectural Services).

q: Determining the adequate size and appropriate configuration and assemblage for a proposed project in consideration of the use, allocation and interface of spaces for given activities
n: Space planning determines the adequate size, configuration and assemblage of spaces for given activities, based on their use, allocation and interface. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 201, Sec. 2.8.

q: A developer intends to construct a 40-storey mixed-use tower using conventional structural engineering principles. Instead of the typical reinforced concrete system previously used by the design team, the project adopts Cross-Laminated Timber (CLT) floor plates and wall panels. While the building continues to perform the same structural functions and follows the same basic load-transfer principles, the adoption of CLT requires substantial changes to the manner by which building components are connected, assembled, detailed, and integrated throughout the project. According to innovation theory, what type of Innovation is BEST represented by this change?
n: Henderson and Clark call it architectural innovation when the core design concepts stay the same but the way components are linked and integrated changes. Here the structural function and load path are unchanged, but CLT changes how parts connect and assemble. Source: Henderson, R. M. & Clark, K. B. (1990), "Architectural Innovation," Administrative Science Quarterly 35(1).

q: The architect studies how spaces relate to one another, how users move through the project, and how activities are organized before any detailed design solution is prepared. Which architectural planning consideration is MOST fundamental?
o: Functional relationships and circulation between spaces
Open floor plans with minimal partitions
n: Before detailed design, the most basic planning consideration is the functional relationships and circulation between spaces, typically studied through adjacency matrices and bubble diagrams. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 201, Architectural Programming; White, E. T., Space Adjacency Analysis.

q: Under the Scope of Pre-Design Services in SPP Document 201, which activity involves the architect stating the project Terms of Reference (TOR), including the concept, objectives, and other necessary requirements for bidding out architectural services?
n: In design brief preparation the architect sets out the project terms of reference (ToR), including the concept, objectives and other requirements, for bidding out architectural services. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 201, Sec. 2.11.

q: Which of the following best describes the scope of services under SPP Document 201 as defined in the IRR of R.A. No. 9266?
o: Pre-design services including feasibility studies, site analysis, and architectural programming
Structural engineering and mechanical systems design
Architectural design and construction supervision services
n: SPP Doc. 201 covers Pre-Design Services: consultation, pre-feasibility and feasibility studies, site selection and analysis, site utilization, architectural research, programming, space planning and design brief preparation. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 201, Sec. 2.

q: In the context of an architect's engagement, which activity under SPP Document 201 comes first and is recognized as the architect's initial professional service?
n: Consultation (Sec. 2.1) is the first pre-design service listed. In it the architect gives oral or written advice to a prospective client, whether or not the project proceeds. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 201, Sec. 2.1.
